result.note: Tests the February 2026 three-hour deepfake takedown window and the elements of MeitY's August 2026 directive to Meta.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) set a window within which platforms must take down deepfakes. What was that window?
questions.explain: MeitY gave platforms three hours to take down deepfakes in February 2026. This followed amendments to India's IT Intermediary Rules that tightened due-diligence requirements and raised platform accountability for AI-generated content.
questions.source: MeitY gave platforms a three hour window to take down deepfakes back in February

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) issued directions to Meta on content moderation. Consider the following statements:
items: Meta was directed to submit a roadmap to curb deepfakes, propaganda and synthetic content across its platforms.
Meta was asked to strictly adhere to data-localisation rules and speed up the execution of government takedown requests.
In talks with ministry officials, Meta acknowledged technical gaps in handling child sex abuse material and deepfakes.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. MeitY also wants Meta to re-engineer its algorithms to throttle the reach of manipulated media, though TBB notes such automated filters can also catch legitimate speech, news and satire.
questions.source: Meta must strengthen moderation, accelerate the execution of government takedown requests, strictly adhere to data-localization rules, and re-engineer algorithms to actively throttle the reach of manipulated media.
